newsitem.title: JORDAN: Violence breaks out at Jordan soccer match.
newsitem.headline: Violence breaks out at Jordan soccer match.

text.p: Jordanian soccer fans hurled stones and bottles and smashed car windows as a showdown between two top clubs turned violent, newspapers said on Saturday.

They said clashes broke out during the match between Faisali and Wihdat, both undefeated before Friday's encounter, and spread outside the stadium in Amman's Sports City complex after the match, which Faisali won 1-0.
One witness told Reuters the Wihdat fans, mostly from a Palestinian refugee camp on the fringes of Amman, accused the referee of bias.

He said they started shouting slogans supporting Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat and attacking the Jordanian government. The clashes broke out at half time as supporters started throwing glass bottles and stones at each other.

At the end of the match police intervened to get Wihdat fans, the majority of the 25,000 attendance, out of the stadium. Wihdat supporters then threw stones at the police. Fans then started attacking cars and nearby shops, the witness said.
Al-Rai newspaper quoted Minister of Youth Mohammad Daoudieh as saying fans damaged a theatre and another nearby stadium, as well as smashing car windows and other property.
Witnesses said ambulances took injured fans to hospital and the official Petra News Agency said a number of arrests were made. It gave no details.

Soccer violence in Jordan is rare but passions frequently run high in the keenly contested matches between Faisali and the mainly Palestinian Wihdat. Faisali's win on Friday put it top of Jordan's Premier League, one point ahead of Wihdat.
